stories.headline: Field Marshal Munir leads Pakistan's US-Iran mediation from Tehran, ISPR announces 'encouraging progress'
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir made two visits to Tehran (May 22–23), meeting Iranian President Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf, and Foreign Minister Araghchi. Pakistan's ISPR announced 'encouraging progress toward a final understanding' on a US-Iran MoU; Trump separately described a deal as 'largely negotiated.' The visits — partly preceded by reports of postponement — placed Munir as the primary interlocutor between Washington and Tehran, alongside Qatar. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi conducted parallel shuttle diplomacy. PM Shehbaz Sharif praised Munir's role and said Pakistan hoped to host the next round of talks 'very soon.'

stories.headline: BLA suicide bombing kills at least 24 on military train in Quetta ahead of Eid
stories.summary: A suicide bomber detonated an explosives-laden vehicle near a railway track in Quetta as a passenger train carrying military personnel and their families passed on Sunday, May 24. The Baloch Liberation Army's Majeed Brigade claimed responsibility. The death toll was reported variously at 14–24+, with over 70 wounded. President Zardari, PM Shehbaz, and Balochistan authorities condemned the attack; Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi travelled to Quetta.

stories.headline: PM Shehbaz Sharif makes four-day China visit, signs $1.22B+ in investment deals, meets Xi Jinping
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif visited China from May 23–26, beginning in Hangzhou (B2B investment conference, meetings with tech CEOs, MoUs worth over $7B signed) before moving to Beijing for meetings with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang. Discussions covered CPEC Phase II, agriculture, IT, renewables, and Pakistan's mediation role in the Iran-US conflict. The visit coincided with the 75th anniversary of Pakistan-China diplomatic relations.

stories.headline: Leaked cypher renews scrutiny of US role in Imran Khan's 2022 ouster; PTI protests continue
stories.summary: Investigative outlet Drop Site published Cable I-0678 — the classified Pakistani diplomatic telegram Imran Khan cited as evidence of a US-backed conspiracy to remove him — prompting wide coverage. PTI and allied TTAP staged countrywide protests demanding Khan's release and medical care; opposition leader Achakzai threatened budget boycott. Separate reporting raised concerns about Khan's eyesight deteriorating in solitary confinement.
